note: Faithful rendering of the stages of faith and the instruction for stabilizing it; only loose phrasing, nothing a specialist would need to correct.

errors.english: "For the purpose of knowing" implies
errors.why: rig phyir is the lemma 'because it is experienced/cognized', a reason clause, not a purpose.

note: Difficult dream/pramāṇa argument tracked reasonably; one lemma misread as a purpose clause.

errors.english: Except for those that do not produce filth
errors.why: The subject (srog chags, from the previous side) is living creatures: except where creatures have not arisen, the grass is to be discarded; 'filth' is not in the text.

errors.english: bundles of grass should be spread out, tied with ropes, and left suspended from trees
errors.why: The bundles are to be tied and hung in trees until the time they are spread on the walkway, not spread out and then hung.

errors.english: Materials for cleaning such as dung
errors.why: 'dag rdzas is plastering/floor-smearing material; the dung is kept on potsherds as material for plaster, not as a cleaning agent.

errors.english: You will also be free from the burdens of managing bowls, robes, nets, bowls, belts, receiving transmissions, reading, reciting, yoga, and mental cultivation.
errors.why: The Vinaya formula is a promise that the novices will not lack (be well provided with) bowls, robes, instruction, recitation, yoga and attention, not that they will be freed from them.

errors.english: made them establish residences for him
errors.why: gnas 'cha' ba is taking niśraya (formal dependence): Udāyin had them take dependence on him.

fix.find: made them establish residences for him
fix.replace: had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: After Udayin and each of them had received their respective lodgings and sat down
errors.why: The attendants received lodgings for Udāyin and for themselves; Udāyin was still outside and received nothing.

note: Usable Vinaya narrative, but niśraya and several practical details of the bedding rule and the Udāyin story are misread.

errors.english: the youth Dawa Moon
errors.why: In a jātaka translated from Sanskrit the prince's name should be given as Candra, not a Tibetan transliteration doubled with its gloss.

errors.english: For why do men, even if born from a great lineage, come to be seen as equal to a dog?
errors.why: gang phyir is causal ('for men, though born of great families, are seen to be like dogs'), a statement, not a question.

errors.english: Those who have not generated qualities,
errors.why: The verse says merit does not lie in birth (ancestry): even glass may hold the sapphire's colour; the English invents 'those who have not generated qualities' and turns the final line into a question.

errors.english: the name of the holder of the piece
errors.why: dum bu 'dzin pa is the proper name of the person (the one who later grows angry and plots), rendered throughout as a description.

errors.english: Dawa is captivating and separated from...
errors.why: The plotter says Candra must by some means be separated from Yid 'phrog (the domain/what he has captured), not that Candra is captivating.

note: The narrative thread is followable but names, the verses and the plotter's speech are badly misconstrued.

errors.english: when we later explain the destruction of a pot and so forth
errors.why: 'chad par 'gyur ba here means 'when a pot etc. is cut off/ceases', not 'when we later explain'.

note: Sound rendering of the two kinds of destruction and of contradiction as gradual diminution; one verb misread.

errors.english: such as a vase or sound, one might argue
errors.why: The Tibetan simply gives the example of the space-proponent's syllogism; 'vase or sound' and the framing as an opponent's argument are added.

errors.english: is "by one's own soul"
errors.why: bdag nyid glosses svayam as 'oneself'; 'soul' imports an ātman sense absent here.

errors.english: during a debate the treatise itself is not the primary thing being accepted
errors.why: The lemma 'even though a treatise is accepted' is glossed: at the time of debate a treatise is not to be accepted at all; the English softens this to 'not the primary thing'.

note: The svayam discussion is followed correctly in outline, with a few softened or padded glosses.

errors.english: the logical absurdity that it would reside within itself would follow without hindrance
errors.why: The consequence that applies is the question 'where would it itself reside?', i.e. there is no place left for the whole, not that it resides in itself.

fix.find: the logical absurdity that it would reside within itself would follow without hindrance
fix.replace: the absurd consequence, "where then would it itself reside?", applies without hindrance

errors.english: there would be no room for the parts themselves
errors.why: It is the whole that would find no room in the parts, not the parts that lack room.

errors.english: Because it is not connected to many, it would become many; otherwise, it could not be one.
errors.why: Being connected with many it would be many, so it cannot otherwise be one; the English inserts a negation.

fix.find: Because it is not connected to many, it would become many; otherwise, it could not be one.
fix.replace: Because it is connected to many, it would be many; it could not otherwise be one.

note: The avayavin refutation is mostly readable, but two key consequences are inverted or misstated.

span_why: The opening of the side (from ལྟོས་པ་ནི་དེར་ངེས་པར་མི་རུང་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ to གཞན་དུ་ན་དོན་ལན་འགའ་ཡང་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ, on smoke being fixed in place and time to its producer) is not translated.

errors.english: If the head of (Indra) the king of gods
errors.why: śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is Dharmakīrti's stock term for an anthill, not Indra's literal head.

fix.find: If the head of (Indra) the king of gods

errors.english: from slightly heavy [note: earthly] elements
errors.why: lci ba is cow dung, the standard example of a heterogeneous source from which lotus-type plants are seen to arise.

note: Argument on fixed causal natures is followed, but the opening is missing and two stock Pramāṇa examples are mistranslated.

errors.english: although the object of sound does not have a nature of various conjunctions
errors.why: sgra'i yul is the literal referent of the word: although conjunction is not literally variegated, it is called so figuratively; 'sound' is wrong.

errors.english: because of the "inherence" [note: original: "samavaya"] of many things into a single object of conjunction
errors.why: The proposal is that the conjunction inheres in a single object (the painting), not that many things inhere in an object of conjunction.

note: Vaiśeṣika citrabuddhi debate rendered competently; two clauses of the opponent's view are skewed.

errors.english: it is impossible for them to possess number, because number and possession
errors.why: ldan pa here is the Vaiśeṣika quality conjunction (saṃyoga), listed with number (saṃkhyā) as two guṇas found only in substances.

fix.find: it is impossible for them to possess number, because number and possession
fix.replace: number and conjunction (saṃyoga) are likewise impossible for them, because number and conjunction

errors.english: Regarding the other position, the author states "Now..." and so forth.
errors.why: gzhan gyis marks the opponent as the one who says 'now…', not the author.

note: Clear and accurate on the regress of natures and the six padārthas, apart from saṃyoga and the final speaker.
